{{proposal}}
=== <span class="anchor" id="G15"></span><span class="anchor" id="g15"></span>G15. LLM-generated pages without human review ===
{{Shortcut|WP:G15}}
This applies to any page (including previous revisions that are substantially similar) that exhibits any of the three following signs which indicate that the page could only plausibly have been generated by [[large language model]]s (LLM)<ref>Technology behind [[AI chatbot]]s such as [[ChatGPT]] and [[Google Gemini]]</ref> and would have been removed by any ''reasonable human review'':<ref>Here, "reasonable human review" means that a human editor has 1) thoroughly read and edited the LLM-generated text and 2) verified that the generated citations exist and verify corresponding content. For example, even a brand new editor would recognize that a user-aimed message like "I hope this helps!" is wholly inappropriate for inclusion if they had read the page carefully.{{pb}}In article space, even if someone had conducted a reasonable review, the [[Wikipedia:Writing articles with large language models|use of LLMs to generate or rewrite content is prohibited]]; this, however, does not influence this speedy deletion criterion (and vice versa—this criterion encompassing the standard of "reasonable human review" does not mean that meeting the same standard can surmount the prohibition).</ref>  
* '''Communication intended for the user''': This may include collaborative communication (e.g., "Here is your Wikipedia article on..."),<ref>Note that user-facing instructions may be present in infoboxes, especially older ones. For example, articles with [[Template:Infobox military person]] often contain the boilerplate "Add spouse if reliably sourced".</ref> knowledge-cutoff disclaimers (e.g., "Up to my last training update ..."), self-insertion (e.g., "as a large language model"), and [[Wikipedia:AIPLACEHOLDER|unfilled placeholders]] (e.g., "Smith was born on [Birth Date]" rather than the person's actual birth date).<ref>Note that placeholders also appear on human-made [[:Category:Article creation templates|article templates]] such as [[Template:Biography]], the use of which are not signs of LLM generation.</ref>
* '''Non-existent or nonsensical references''': This may include external links that are [[Wikipedia:Link rot|dead]] on arrival, [[ISBN]]s with invalid [[checksum]]s, unresolvable or unrelated [[Digital Object Identifiers|DOI]]s, and citations that exhibit invalid [[temporality]] (e.g. news reports about an accident before the accident occurred) or incorrect metadata, such as misattributed authors. To rule out other causes like typos or [[link rot]], tagging editors should consult the [[Wayback Machine]] and not take a single example as definitive.<ref>For example, seemingly dead-on-arrival links may have been [[geoblock]]ed in your region or copied from another article.</ref> When a page includes a large number of references, the references of concern should be noted in the rationale.
* '''Technical indicators''': This may include [[Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing#turn0search0|model-specific citation bugs]] like the insertion of <code>oaicite</code>, <code>attributionIndex</code> JSON blocks, or <code>turn0search0</code>, as well as the presence of <code>```wikitext</code> or <code>```wiki</code> markdown code blocks ([[Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing/Wikitext wrapped in Markdown code blocks from chatbots|additional explanation]]). 

In addition to the clear-cut signs listed above, there are other, more subjective [[Wikipedia:AISIGNS|signs of LLM writing]] that may also plausibly stem from human error or unfamiliarity with Wikipedia's [[Wikipedia:PAG|policies and guidelines]]. While these indicators can be used in conjunction, ''they should not serve as the sole basis for applying this criterion''. For less clear-cut cases, consider starting a discussion at the [[Wikipedia:AI noticeboard|AI noticeboard]] or [[Wikipedia:Articles for deletion|Articles for deletion]].  

* {{Tl|Db-g15}}, {{Tl|Db-ai}}, {{Tl|Db-llm}}
* {{clc|Candidates for speedy deletion as unreviewed LLM-generated content}}
